# Story 16 — App Shell Navigation: Breadcrumbs & Sidebar Profile Placement

## Prerequisites

- Story 15 (Platform administration surface) completed in this working tree. All 7 `/admin/*` routes (`users`, `audit-log`, `departments`, `branches`, `branding`, `sla-targets`, `reminder-lead-time`) are already declared in `frontend/src/routes/AppRouter.tsx` and reachable through the sidebar `NAV_ITEMS` in `frontend/src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx`.
- Frontend-only story. No coordination with backend owners required. No new dependencies added to `frontend/package.json` — `react-router-dom` v6.30 already ships `Route.handle` + `useMatches()`.
- No frontend test runner exists in this project; verification is manual (same convention as Stories 4–15).

---

## Story Goal

Give staff (Agent/Admin) users a persistent sense of location and a consistent path to their account/logout across the 20+ authenticated routes rendered inside `AppShell.tsx`, by:

1. Adding **one** reusable breadcrumb bar to the shared shell, driven by route metadata declared once in `AppRouter.tsx` (not by copy-pasted per-page code).
2. Letting detail pages (`CustomerDetailPage.tsx`, `TicketDetailPage.tsx`) publish a dynamic label for the current crumb (customer name, ticket subject) so the raw `:id` segment never appears.
3. Moving the existing profile/logout block from the bottom (`mt-auto`) to the top of the sidebar `<aside>`, reusing the same `useAuthStore` data and `handleLogout` handler already in `AppShell.tsx` — not a second copy.

**Not in scope:** `PortalShell.tsx` and `/portal/*` routes; changing any nav item / `adminOnly` gating; the pre-existing header logout icon (`AppShell.tsx` ~line 143); `document.title`; any backend change.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** Every page renders its own `<h1>` and (for detail pages) hand-rolls a "back to list" link. Profile block sits at the bottom of the sidebar. No breadcrumb exists anywhere.
- **New behaviour:** One breadcrumb bar is rendered by `AppShell.tsx` above `<Outlet />` on every authenticated route. Route hierarchy and static labels come from a single declaration in `AppRouter.tsx` (`Route.handle`). Detail pages publish a dynamic last-crumb label via a shared hook. The profile block moves to the **top** of the sidebar `<aside>`; the header logout icon is left alone. Existing per-page `<h1>` headings stay — this story does not remove them.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Introduce the breadcrumb data model

**Create file:** `frontend/src/routes/breadcrumbs.ts`

Define the shape of route-handle metadata and the shared type used by the shell and the dynamic-label hook:

```ts
export type BreadcrumbHandle = {
  /** i18n key for the static label of this route (e.g. 'shell.breadcrumb.tickets'). */
  labelKey: string;
  /** Absolute path of the parent crumb, or null when this route is a top-level page. */
  parentPath: string | null;
  /**
   * When true, the label for this crumb is expected to be supplied dynamically by the
   * rendered page (via useBreadcrumbLabel). If the page has not yet published a label,
   * the parent's labelKey is shown instead — the raw :id must never be rendered.
   */
  dynamic?: boolean;
};
```

Export a small type guard `isBreadcrumbHandle(handle: unknown): handle is BreadcrumbHandle` that the shell can use to narrow `match.handle` from `useMatches()`.

### 3 — Build the shared breadcrumb hook + component

**Create file:** `frontend/src/components/layout/useBreadcrumbLabel.ts`

A tiny context-backed hook:

```ts
import { createContext, useContext, useEffect } from 'react';

export type BreadcrumbLabelSetter = (label: string | null) => void;
export const BreadcrumbLabelContext = createContext<BreadcrumbLabelSetter | null>(null);

/**
 * Detail pages call this once their entity has loaded to publish the current
 * (last) crumb's label. Pass null (or omit the call) while data is loading —
 * the breadcrumb will fall back to the parent's label, never showing the raw :id.
 */
export function useBreadcrumbLabel(label: string | null | undefined): void {
  const setter = useContext(BreadcrumbLabelContext);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!setter) return;
    setter(label ?? null);
    return () => setter(null);
  }, [setter, label]);
}
```

**Create file:** `frontend/src/components/layout/Breadcrumbs.tsx`

- Consumes `useMatches()` from `react-router-dom`; filters matches whose `handle` passes `isBreadcrumbHandle`.
- Takes the deepest such match as the "current" route.
- Walks `parentPath` upward, looking each parent up in a route-metadata map built from the same declarations (build it by exporting the array from `AppRouter.tsx` or by a tiny lookup helper alongside `breadcrumbs.ts` — planner's choice; the executor should keep the source of truth single). Stop when `parentPath` is `null`.
- Reverses the collected list so ancestors come first, current last.
- For each ancestor: render a `<Link to={path}>{t(labelKey)}</Link>`.
- For the current (last) crumb:
  - If the route's `handle.dynamic === true` **and** a dynamic label has been published via context state, render that label.
  - If `dynamic === true` **and** no label is published yet, render the parent's translated `labelKey` (never `t(dynamicLabelKey)` alone, and never the raw `:id`).
  - Otherwise render `t(labelKey)`.
  - Mark it with `aria-current="page"`, non-interactive (`<span>`, not `<Link>`), and a distinct style (e.g. `font-medium text-slate-900`).
- Separator: a translated symbol from `t('shell.breadcrumb.separator')` (default `'/'`) rendered inside a `<span aria-hidden="true">`. Use logical spacing (`ms-2 me-2` or `gap-2` on the flex container) so RTL flips automatically via `document.documentElement.dir`. **No** `if (isRtl)` branching.
- Container: `<nav aria-label={t('shell.breadcrumb.ariaLabel')} className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2 text-sm text-slate-500">…</nav>`. `flex-wrap` satisfies FR6.
- When only one crumb exists (top-level page), render just that crumb (AC2 — no invented parent).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Detail page navigated to directly (deep link).** `useBreadcrumbLabel` is called only after the entity fetch resolves. Until then, `Breadcrumbs.tsx` renders the parent label (e.g. "Tickets") in place of the missing dynamic crumb — never the raw `:id`. Enforced in `Breadcrumbs.tsx` (task 3) and by passing `null` while `ticket` / `customer` state is still `undefined` in the detail pages (task 6).
- **Route without `handle` metadata.** If a future route is added without a `BreadcrumbHandle`, `Breadcrumbs.tsx` filters it out via `isBreadcrumbHandle` (task 1) and shows nothing rather than crashing.
- **Orphaned `parentPath`.** If a `parentPath` in `AppRouter.tsx` does not resolve to a known route (typo), the walker stops and renders whatever chain it has so far. Executor must double-check that every `parentPath` string in task 2 matches an existing `path=` string exactly.
- **Dynamic label bleed across navigations.** Solved by `setDynamicLabel(null)` in the existing location-change `useEffect` in `AppShell.tsx` (task 4). Without this, navigating from `/tickets/1` to `/customers` could briefly show a stale ticket subject.
- **Long labels on narrow viewports.** Container uses `flex-wrap` and `text-sm` (task 3); the trail wraps to a second line rather than pushing header content off-screen (AC10).
- **RTL.** No component-level `if (isRtl)` — layout relies on Tailwind logical utilities (`ms-*` / `me-*` / `gap-*` / `flex-wrap`) and on the global `document.documentElement.dir` set by `LanguageProvider.tsx`. Separators render inside `aria-hidden` spans so screen readers announce only labels.
- **Role filtering unchanged.** `visibleNavItems` at `AppShell.tsx:44` is not touched; a non-Admin still cannot see or reach `/admin/*` in the nav. Direct URL access continues to be gated by whatever page-level guards exist today (this story does not add any).
- **Duplicate logout.** The header logout icon at `AppShell.tsx:143` is intentionally left in place per intake §8. Post-change, `handleLogout` (defined once at line 71) must still be referenced by exactly two `onClick` handlers — the relocated sidebar button and the header icon.

## Test Plan

No automated frontend test runner exists in this project (intake §8 confirms and forbids introducing one). Verification is manual, matching Stories 4–15.

1. **Manual route sweep (LTR / English):** visit each of the 21 authenticated routes listed in AC1 and confirm the breadcrumb trail is correct and the last crumb has `aria-current="page"` (inspect via DevTools).
2. **Deep-link detail pages:** open `/customers/:id` and `/tickets/:id` directly in a fresh tab; confirm the last crumb shows the parent label ("Customers" / "Tickets") during the fetch and switches to the entity name once loaded, **never** showing the raw id (AC6, AC7).
3. **Navigation from ancestor crumb:** on `/reports/sla`, click "Reports" — location changes to `/reports` and the trail updates (AC4).
4. **RTL sweep (Arabic):** switch language to Arabic via `LanguageToggle`, revisit at least Home, `/tickets`, `/tickets/:id`, `/reports/sla`, `/admin/users`; confirm crumb order, separators, and the profile block layout all read right-to-left correctly (AC9).
5. **Mobile viewport:** at ≤ `lg` breakpoint, confirm the breadcrumb bar wraps rather than clipping the current page's label and the current page label is still visible (AC10). Confirm the sidebar drawer opens via hamburger, closes on backdrop click, Escape, and route change (AC15) on Home, `/tickets`, `/admin/users`.
6. **Role filtering regression:** log in as a non-Admin agent; confirm the seven `/admin/*` items and the three `adminOnly` items (`webhooks`, `reports`, `api-keys`) are still hidden from `visibleNavItems` (AC14).
7. **Grep audits:**
   - `` grep -r "Breadcrumb" frontend/src/pages `` — must return zero matches (AC1).
   - `` grep -rn "handleLogout" frontend/src `` — must return exactly the same file (`AppShell.tsx`) and count of definitions as before, with only the two existing `onClick` references (AC12).
8. **i18n parity:** run whatever `check_i18n_parity`-style diff the project uses (or manually diff key sets under `shell.breadcrumb` in `en.json` and `ar.json`) — zero missing keys on either side (AC8).

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend builds:** in `frontend/`, run `npm install` (if lockfile changed — it should not) and `npm run build`. Build must succeed with no TypeScript errors introduced by the new `handle` typings on `<Route>` (React Router v6 types accept `handle: unknown` — the `BreadcrumbHandle` type is applied inside `Breadcrumbs.tsx` via `isBreadcrumbHandle`).
2. **Frontend runs:** `npm run dev` in `frontend/`, log in as an Admin, walk the AC1 route list once in English and once in Arabic. Then log in as a non-Admin agent and confirm role-filtered nav visibility (AC14).
3. **Backend builds:** no backend change expected. As a safety check, `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCrm.sln` should still succeed unchanged.
4. **Regression — scoped diff:** `git diff --stat` must show changes only under `frontend/src/components/layout/`, `frontend/src/routes/`, `frontend/src/pages/CustomerDetailPage.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/TicketDetailPage.tsx`, and `frontend/src/i18n/locales/{en,ar}.json`. Any change outside this set is a scope violation (AC16, DoD final bullet).
